question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\,k \\  & =2x\,i+2y\,j+4z\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t+1,$ $y=t-1$ and $z=\operatorname{sin}⁡t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2(t+1)\,i+2(t-1)\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =i+j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2(t+1)\,i+2(t-1)\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k)\cdot (i+j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k) \\  & =2(t+1)\cdot 1+2(t-1)\cdot 1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =2t+2+2t-2+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =4(t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$
